Mène la feature suivante avec l'équipe d'agents : 210

Délègue chaque étape à l'agent indiqué (outil Agent) ; ne fais pas le travail toi-même.
Une étape peut être sautée si elle n'apporte rien : dis-le et pourquoi.

**Suivi** : si `210` est un identifiant Plane (ex. `DEVDESK-12`) et que les outils
`mcp__plane-orchestrator__*` sont disponibles, charge la skill
`plane-integration:plane-conventions` et suis la section « Suivi dans Plane » de l'agent
`team-core:orchestrator` : tu joues l'orchestrator, n'écris qu'avec
`mcp__plane-orchestrator__*` (tâches, assignations, états, comptes rendus), et transmets
l'identifiant au `reviewer`, au `tester` et à `devops`, qui commentent eux-mêmes.

**Avancement** : charge la skill `team-core:resume-work` et tiens à jour
`.agent-progress/<ID>.md` à chaque sous-étape, pour pouvoir reprendre avec `/resume` après
une coupure.

**Ne rien supposer** : un brief ambigu ou un choix qui appartient à l'utilisateur lui est
posé (`AskUserQuestion` pour un choix entre options). Quand un agent rend des **Questions
bloquantes**, pose-les à l'utilisateur sans y répondre à sa place, note les réponses dans
le fichier d'avancement, puis relance l'agent avec elles.

**Sobriété** : demande à chaque agent un compte rendu court (résultat, fichiers touchés,
points ouverts ; pas de journal de ce qu'il a lu). Les tests ciblés pendant les étapes ; la suite
complète une fois, à la fin. Un seul `coder` à la fois sauf
étapes réellement indépendantes.

1. **Cadrage** — lis la story : `workitem retrieve_by_identifier` (Plane) ou
   `gh issue view` (numéro d'issue GitHub). Si les critères d'acceptation manquent ou sont
   flous, `product-team:pm` les précise. Soumets les questions ouvertes à l'utilisateur
   avant de continuer.
2. **Conception** — `dev-team:architect` : plan en étapes livrables (sauf changement
   local et évident). Si `LLM_WIKI_PATHS` est défini (`printenv LLM_WIKI_PATHS`) et que la
   conception est structurante (nouveau composant, bibliothèque, sécurité, données),
   lance d'abord `dev-team:wiki-scout` avec le sujet et passe sa synthèse dans le brief
   de l'architecte. Fais valider le plan par l'utilisateur.
3. **Réalisation en TDD**, pour chaque étape du plan :
   - **rouge** — `dev-team:tester` écrit les tests de l'étape (critères, interfaces et
     comportements du plan) et montre qu'ils échouent pour la bonne raison. Étape sans
     test pertinent (config, infra, doc) : il le dit, passe directement au `coder` ;
   - **vert puis refactorisation** — `dev-team:coder` reçoit les fichiers de test et la
     commande, écrit le code minimal qui les fait passer, puis refactorise ;
   - `dev-team:reviewer` relit code et tests (+ `dev-team:security-reviewer` si auth,
     données sensibles, entrées externes ou dépendances) ;
   - points bloquants → retour au `coder` (deux allers-retours maximum, puis remonte
     le désaccord à l'utilisateur) ;
   - relance toi-même la commande de tests ciblés de l'étape et constate le vert.
   Après la dernière étape : `dev-team:tester` en mode vérification (suite complète,
   couverture des critères d'acceptation).
4. **Documentation** — `team-core:tech-writer` si le comportement visible change ;
   `team-core:archivist` si une décision a été prise ou si `CLAUDE.md` doit évoluer.
5. **Livraison** — propose à l'utilisateur de faire créer la branche et la PR par
   `dev-team:devops`.

Termine par : ce qui est fait, comment c'est vérifié (résultats de tests observés),
ce qui reste, les risques. Si une autre story suit, suggère `/clear` avant de la lancer. Une fois la PR créée,
supprime le fichier d'avancement (en le disant).

Base directory for this skill: /home/anthoni/.claude/plugins/cache/anthnel-agents/team-core/0.12.2/skills/resume-work

# Avancement et reprise

Une session peut s'arrêter à tout moment (limite d'usage, `/clear`, plantage). Le fichier
d'avancement permet de repartir de la bonne étape sans relire toute l'histoire.

## Emplacement

`.agent-progress/<ID>.md` à la racine du dépôt, où `<ID>` est l'identifiant de la story
ou du bug (`DEVDESK-12`, `gh-15`) ou, sans identifiant, un slug court
(`fix-timeout-export`).

Ce dossier ne doit jamais être commité. Au premier usage, vérifie que `.gitignore`
contient `.agent-progress/` ; sinon ajoute la ligne (ou, si tu ne peux pas écrire,
demande à l'utilisateur de le faire).

## Quand l'écrire

Remplace le fichier entier (pas d'historique, il doit rester court) :
- après validation du plan par l'utilisateur ;
- à chaque fin de sous-étape (rouge, vert, revue, tests constatés) ;
- quand une question est posée à l'utilisateur, et quand il y répond ;
- avant de rendre la main en fin de session.

## Format (40 lignes au plus)

```markdown
# <ID> — <titre>
Commande : /feature | /bugfix — Mis à jour : AAAA-MM-JJ HH:MM
Branche : <nom> — Plane : <ID ou —>

## Plan
1. [x] <étape> — tests verts (`<commande>`)
2. [~] <étape> — rouge fait (`<fichiers de test>`), vert en cours
3. [ ] <étape>

## Étape en cours
Sous-étape : rouge | vert | revue | tests | doc | livraison
Commande de tests ciblés : `<commande>`
Dernier résultat observé : <n passés / n échoués> (AAAA-MM-JJ HH:MM)

## Décisions et réponses de l'utilisateur
- <décision courte> (pourquoi en quelques mots)

## Points ouverts
- <question en attente, désaccord coder ↔ reviewer, risque>

## Prochaine action
<une phrase : quel agent, avec quel brief>
```

Le plan détaillé reste dans le compte rendu de l'architecte ou dans Plane : ici, une ligne
par étape suffit. Pas de sortie d'agent recopiée.

## Reprendre (`/resume`)

1. Lis `.agent-progress/<ID>.md`. Sans identifiant, liste le dossier ; s'il y en a
   plusieurs, demande lequel reprendre.
2. Confronte le fichier à la réalité, sans tout relire :
   - `git branch --show-current` et `git status --short` : bonne branche, fichiers
     attendus ;
   - `git diff --stat` : ampleur du travail non commité ;
   - relance la commande de tests ciblés de l'étape en cours et compare au dernier
     résultat noté.
3. En cas d'écart (autre branche, tests dans un état différent, fichiers inattendus),
   décris-le à l'utilisateur et demande comment continuer. Ne devine pas.
4. Sinon, résume en trois lignes où on en est et la prochaine action, puis reprends le
   déroulé de `/feature` ou `/bugfix` à cette sous-étape.

## Fin

Quand la story est livrée (PR créée) ou abandonnée, supprime le fichier, après l'avoir dit
à l'utilisateur.

Base directory for this skill: /home/anthoni/.claude/plugins/cache/anthnel-agents/plane-integration/0.12.2/skills/plane-conventions # Conventions Plane ## Identités Chaque rôle écrit dans Plane sous son propre compte, via son propre serveur MCP. **N'utilise que le serveur du rôle que tu joues à cette étape.** | Rôle | Serveur MCP | Écrit | |---|---|---| | pm | `plane-pm` | Modules (epics), stories, priorités, liens vers brief/stories | | orchestrator | `plane-orchestrator` | Tâches, bugs, assignations, états (sauf Done d'une story), comptes rendus des agents sans jeton | | reviewer | `plane-reviewer` | Commentaire de revue | | tester | `plane-tester` | Commentaire de résultats de tests | | devops | `plane-devops` | Lien vers la PR, story en Done après merge | Les comptes architect, coder, debugger, security, techwriter et ux n'ont pas de jeton : on leur **assigne** des tâches, l'orchestrator commente pour eux. Dans la session principale : `/idea` joue le rôle pm, `/feature` et `/bugfix` le rôle orchestrator, `/plane-setup` le rôle orchestrator. Le serveur `plane` (jeton personnel de l'utilisateur), s'il existe, n'est jamais utilisé par les agents. ## Contexte du dépôt Lis la section `## Plane` du `CLAUDE.md` du dépôt : workspace, projet, identifiants des états, labels et membres. Absente → propose `/plane-setup ` et n'écris rien dans Plane avant. ## Modèle | Concept | Plane | |---|---| | Epic | **Module** (`module create`, puis `module manage_workitems add_ids=…`) | | Story | Work item, label `story`, rattaché à son module | | Tâche | Work item, label `task`, `parent=` | | Bug | Work item, label `bug` (parent = story concernée si elle existe) | | Sprint | Cycle | | MoSCoW | Priorité : Must → `high`, Should → `medium`, Could → `low` ; Won't → pas de work item | | Effort S/M/L | Ligne `Effort : M` dans la description | Description d'une story (`description_html`) : ```html

Story

En tant que …, je veux … afin de …

Critères d'acceptation

  • Given … When … Then …

Contexte

Effort : M — Brief : docs/product/<idée>/brief.md

``` ## États `Backlog` (créée par pm) → `Todo` (validée, prête) → `In Progress` (coder/debugger au travail) → `In Review` (reviewer/tester) → `Done` · `Cancelled`. - Tâche : l'orchestrator la passe en `Done` quand le tester a validé. - Story : `devops` la passe en `Done` après le merge de la PR. ## Règles - **Lire une story** par son identifiant : `workitem retrieve_by_identifier` (`DEVDESK-12`). - **Réserver avant de démarrer** (plusieurs sessions peuvent tourner en parallèle) : relis la story ; si elle est déjà In Progress ou In Review, arrête-toi et demande à l'utilisateur. Sinon passe-la en In Progress **avant** tout autre travail. - **Erreur 429** (trop de requêtes, limite par jeton) : attends quelques secondes et réessaie une fois ; ne boucle pas. - **Chercher avant de créer** : `workitem search` (recherche par texte dans les noms, tous projets du workspace) pour éviter les doublons. - **Après chaque assignation, relis le work item** : Plane ignore sans erreur un assigné qui n'est pas membre actif du projet avec le rôle Member. Si l'assigné manque, signale-le (le compte doit être ajouté au projet comme Member). - `member list_project` peut renvoyer d'anciens membres retirés : il ne prouve pas qu'un compte est assignable. - Commentaires en HTML (`

…

`). Mention : `@[]`. Pas de signature : l'auteur est déjà affiché. - **Jamais de suppression ni d'archivage** sans confirmation explicite de l'utilisateur. - Passe toujours `fields` (ex. `id,name,parent,state,assignees,labels`) et `per_page=100` aux `list` pour limiter la taille des réponses ; suis `next_cursor` tant que `next_page_results` est vrai. ## Limites de l'édition Community (constatées) - **Pas de PQL ni de filtres** sur `workitem list` : pour les tâches d'une story, liste les work items du projet et filtre sur `parent` toi-même. - `workitem count`, `workitem_type` (epics natives) : `404`. - Fonctions commerciales indisponibles : `initiative`, `release`, `milestone`, `customer`, teamspaces, types de work item. Ne les appelle pas. ## Sans Plane Si aucun outil `mcp__plane-__*` n'est disponible, utilise GitHub Issues (`gh`) comme avant et signale-le une fois à l'utilisateur.

Story

En tant qu'utilisateur de DevDesk qui le laisse ouvert dans un onglet ou un volet en arrière-plan, je veux que l'application suspende son animation et ses relectures périodiques quand le terminal perd le focus afin d'économiser du CPU, de la batterie et des appels (Docker, transcripts) quand je travaille ailleurs.

Critères d'acceptation

  • Given que le routeur demande les événements de focus (View.ReportFocus, posé par App.View seul) When le terminal perd le focus (BlurMsg) Then la chaîne d'animation partagée (ensureTick : clignotement, spinners) est suspendue, aucun animationTickMsg n'est renouvelé et l'état change dans Update() (Rule 110).
  • Given un terminal sans focus When des relectures périodiques sont actives (:agent-usage toutes les 2 s, statistiques des conteneurs, ports) Then elles sont suspendues ; dans :agent-usage l'en-tête dit « Updates › paused (terminal not focused) » puis « Updates › live » au retour.
  • Given un scan, un clone ou un pull en cours (jobs.Running() supérieur à 0) When le terminal perd le focus Then le job n'est jamais interrompu : seuls le clignotement et les relectures périodiques sont suspendus.
  • Given un job qui échoue pendant le blur When le focus revient Then la mémoire d'échec (jobs.FailureKey) est affichée comme d'habitude, sans échec perdu.
  • Given que le focus revient (FocusMsg) When l'événement arrive Then l'animation reprend, une seule chaîne de tick tourne (pas de multiplication), les vues concernées se relisent une fois, sans re-scan automatique (Rule 126) et sans message de footer (Rule 128 : pas de bruit pour un fait attendu).
  • Given app.motion désactivé When le focus change Then rien ne clignote dans aucun cas.

Dégradation sans support

Given un terminal qui n'envoie jamais BlurMsg (mode 1004 absent, tmux sans focus-events) When l'application tourne Then elle se considère au premier plan et se comporte exactement comme aujourd'hui (test « BlurMsg jamais reçu : comportement identique »). tmux : set -g focus-events on, à documenter dans docs-site.

Règles TUI concernées

Rule 110 (état modifié dans Update seulement), Rule 126 (pas de re-scan automatique), Rule 128 (footer). Le garde activity_guard_test.go ne bouge pas (la phase de clignotement reste lue au rendu).

Contexte

Effort : S pour la seule animation, M avec les relectures et le refresh de retour (livrable en deux temps possibles). Priorité : Should (lot prioritaire, rang 1 du top 5 UX). Vérification manuelle : Windows Terminal et WSL au minimum (décision de l'utilisateur, 2026-11-10). Dépendance DEVDESK-201 (migration Charm v2) : livrée. Hors périmètre : rafraîchir l'état git de ws au retour de O / T. Entrées : docs/ux/bubbletea-v2-improvements.md §2.1 ; .claude/plans/charm-v2-impact.md (§2, §4 F2). Module : Migration Go 1.27 et Charm v2.

Sur `BlurMsg`, on pose le booléen et rien d'autre : le tick déjà en route n'est pas renouvelé et la phase reste sur « on ». Base directory for this skill: /home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.claude/skills/git-worktree-pr

## Work starts in a new worktree

**Any task that will produce a commit begins with its own worktree**, cut from
the current `main`, **under `.worktrees/` inside the repository**:

```bash
git fetch origin main
git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main
cd .worktrees/<branch>
```

Answering a question, reading code, running the app — none of that needs one.
Editing does.

**Under the repository, not beside it.** This reverses what this file said until
now, and the reason it gave was wrong. It claimed a worktree at `.worktrees/x`
would be compiled by `go build ./...` and `go test ./...`. It would not: the go
tool skips every directory whose name begins with `.` or `_`, so `.worktrees/`
is invisible to `./...`. Verified rather than assumed — a package of deliberately
invalid Go placed under `.worktrees/` builds clean and `go list ./...` does not
name it. The old argument holds for `worktrees/` without the dot, which is
presumably where it came from.

What decides it is the **sandbox mount**, and it cost a full debugging session to
find. A direct-mode sandbox mounts *this directory only*. A sibling worktree at
`../devdesk-<branch>` is therefore outside the mount, so its **files** are written
into the container's private layer and never reach the host — while `.git` is
inside the mount and stays shared. Refs agree, files diverge, and nothing warns:
the branch tip moves, the host's copy of those files does not, and `git status`
on the host reports the *stale* content as uncommitted modifications. An agent
and the person testing its work end up compiling different code while both
believe they are on the same branch. Under `.worktrees/`, host and sandbox see
one filesystem.

Two effects worth knowing, neither blocking:

- `.worktrees/` is in `.gitignore`; a worktree there is not a change to the tree.
- Claude Code discovers the nested `.claude/` of each worktree, so its skills and
  rules appear a second time, prefixed by the worktree path. Harmless, and the
  price of the directory being inside the repo.

**What isolates, and what does not.** git refuses to check out one branch in two
worktrees, so two agents cannot land on the same branch by accident — that is the
whole protection, and it is worth knowing what it does *not* cover:

| Shared by every worktree | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `~/.devdesk/` — contexts, `config.yaml`, scan caches | two agents editing settings or scanning at once overwrite each other's; nothing warns |
| the host keyring, Docker, the ports the app binds | one at a time, whoever gets there first |
| `.git/hooks` | verified: `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves to the **main** checkout's, so the Entire checkpoint and pre-push hooks fire normally from a worktree |
| `origin` | inherited — `git push -u origin <branch>` goes through the mirror as usual |

`mise` tasks and `go build` work unchanged; both read the tree they are run in.

**`entire graph` indexes per directory.** A fresh worktree has no index, so the
first `entire graph search` there pays a full build (~5 s on this repo, measured)
and the symbol ids it returns are namespaced by the directory name
(`local/<branch>:Go:…`). Nothing breaks; do not be surprised by the first search
being slow or by ids that do not match another worktree's.

**Clean up when the PR is merged**, from the main checkout:

```bash
git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
git worktree list          # what is still out there
git worktree prune         # after a directory was deleted by hand
```

`git worktree remove` refuses a tree with uncommitted changes, which is the
point — look before forcing.

**The main checkout stays on `main` and stays clean.** It is what `git fetch
origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main` needs after each merge, and what
every new worktree is cut from.

## Git workflow — pull requests only

**Never push directly to `main`.** The Entire mirror rejects it:

```
! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)
```

This is enforced by the mirror, not by GitHub, and **Entire does not document it**
— neither the CLI help nor `docs.entire.io` mentions a protected default branch.
The only branch restriction Entire states is that `entire/unmirrored/*` is never
forwarded. Treat the rejection as observed behaviour, not as a specified one.

**The repository is public since 2026-09-06**, which is what makes GitHub-side
enforcement possible at all: a private repo on a free personal plan answers
`403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public` on both
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main/protection` and
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets` — that was the prior state, and it is not a
description to trust going forward if the repo ever goes private again. Do not
cite `gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main` reporting `"protected":
false` as proof of anything either way: that field only ever reflects legacy
branch protection, so it reads `false` under a ruleset too, and it read `false`
on the free-private plan whatever the configuration. Query
`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets` itself (or `gh ruleset check main`) for the
real answer.

A ruleset named `main-protection` (id `22399372`) now targets `refs/heads/main`
only — deliberately not `entire/checkpoints/v1`, which receives automatic
pushes from the Entire hook and would break if rule-gated. It requires a pull
request (0 approving reviews — solo maintainer, the PR is a record not a review
gate) with the `Lint and build` and `Test` checks from `ci.yml` passing,
blocks force-pushes and branch deletion, and grants no bypass. This closes the
gap the mirror alone left open: the Entire mirror's rejection of a direct push
to `main` was, until now, the *only* protection — a second remote pointing
straight at GitHub would have sailed through (see the warning against adding
one, below). Now GitHub itself refuses that push too.

**The `Entire Gates` check is expected to stay red on this repository.** It is
a PR check from the `entire` app, and its **Approvals** gate fails until another
reviewer approves the trail. That approval cannot arrive: the repository has one
developer, so the gate cannot be green, and no second account or dummy reviewer
should be added to satisfy it. The check is not required by `main-protection`
(GitHub reports the PR as `UNSTABLE` but `MERGEABLE`), so a red `Entire Gates`
alone does not block a merge. Merge once `Lint and build` and `Test` pass. The
Findings, Checks and Up to date gates must stay green: if any of them fails, it
is a real signal, so stop and raise it with the user. Agents (orchestrator,
devops) must not stop to ask for agreement over the Approvals failure alone.
To read the reason:
`gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/commits/<sha>/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="Entire Gates") | .output.summary'`.

Every other branch, including `entire/checkpoints/v1`, pushes through the mirror
and is forwarded to GitHub.

**Pull requests are GitHub's, not Entire's.** Entire has no merge-request
concept — it layers checkpoints and sessions over git and forwards pushes. So
the PR steps below are `gh`, and the branch they review is one `origin` carried
to GitHub. `entire review` (labs) runs a multi-agent review against the current
branch and is a pre-merge step, not a substitute for the PR.

```bash
git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main   # work happens here
git push -u origin <branch>                     # via the mirror — forwarded to GitHub
gh pr create -R anthnel/devdesk --base main --head <branch>
gh pr merge -R anthnel/devdesk <n> --squash --delete-branch
# then, from the main checkout:
git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main   # may need a retry, see below
git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
```

**`-R anthnel/devdesk` is not optional.** `gh` infers the repository from a
remote pointing at a GitHub host, and `origin` is an `entire://` URL, so it
finds none and fails with *"none of the git remotes configured for this
repository point to a known GitHub host"*. The flag names the repo directly.
Do not solve this by adding a GitHub remote — see below.

**After a merge, `origin` can read stale for a minute or two.** The mirror lags
GitHub, so `git fetch origin` right after `gh pr merge` may return the *previous*
`main` — with no error, which is the part that misleads. `gh pr view <n> --json state`
says `MERGED` while `git rev-parse origin/main` still points at the commit before
it. Re-run the fetch a moment later; `gh` is what to trust in the meantime,
because it talks to GitHub directly and needs no remote.

**Do not add a second remote pointing at GitHub to work around that.** The
`main-protection` ruleset (above) would now refuse a direct `git push github
main` too, so it is no longer the *only* defeat of the only protection — but a
direct push still bypasses the mirror, and with it the Entire hook that
records checkpoints and sessions, which is not visible until much later.
`origin` is the only remote, deliberately.

**Merging several branches cut from the same commit conflicts in
`docs/backlog.md`.** Every fix inserts its entry at the top of §1.1, so the
second and third merges land on the same anchor. The resolution is always to
keep both sides — they are independent entries, not competing edits.


**A follow-up commit on the same branch, after the first one already got
squash-merged, will conflict on a plain `git merge`** — squashing rewrites
history, so `git merge origin/main` computes the wrong common ancestor
(the branch's *own* pre-squash parent) and re-diffs files that already
landed, even when nothing actually conflicts in substance. Don't hand-edit
through that; cherry-pick the new commit straight onto current `origin/main`
instead — its real parent already matches what's on `main`, so it applies
clean:

```bash
git worktree add -b <tmp-branch> .worktrees/<tmp-branch> <new-sha>
cd .worktrees/<tmp-branch>
git reset --hard origin/main
git cherry-pick <new-sha>              # clean apply — verify before trusting this
go build ./... && go test ./<touched-packages>/...
git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch-name>
# gh pr create / gh pr merge as above, then from the main checkout:
git worktree remove .worktrees/<tmp-branch>
```

### Remotes

| Remote | URL | Use |
|--------|-----|-----|
| `origin` | `entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/anthnel/devdesk` | Entire mirror — everything: clone, fetch, push |

**There is one remote, and there should stay one.** The repository is hosted on
GitHub and mirrored to EntireDB in `aws-eu-central-1` (a second placement exists
in `aws-us-east-2`), but every git operation goes through the mirror: it is the
regional path, it is what keeps agent reads fast, and it is where the checkpoint
hook runs. Anything needing GitHub's own answer — PR state, review threads —
goes through `gh`, which authenticates directly and does not need a remote.

Semantic search (`entire search`, and the `entire:*` skills that depend on it) is
**not available in the EU region** — the server answers `semantic search is not
yet available in the region(s) hosting this search`. Nothing in the repo config
fixes this.

The sandbox/host relay (landing a sandbox-made commit, developing in the sandbox and testing from the host) is in [sandbox.md](sandbox.md); read it only when a sandbox is involved.

After the merge, load the `release-flow` skill.

## Step 2 — Router → views: `shared.TerminalFocusMsg` (S) — depends on 1

**Files:** `internal/shared/focus.go` (new), `internal/app/focus.go`, `internal/app/jobs.go`
(`enterView` adds `a.sendFocusTo(target)`), `internal/app/app.go` (`reinitializeViews` sends the level to
the rebuilt view on screen). Tests: `internal/app/focus_test.go`.

**Behaviour:**
- Blur edge → the view on screen receives `TerminalFocusMsg{Focused: false}`.
- Focus edge (after a blur) → the view on screen receives `TerminalFocusMsg{Focused: true, Resume: true}`;
  its Cmd is returned. The router itself starts nothing else: no `Init`, no scan request, no footer.
- `enterView` (covers `switchView`, path picker, selection, `scan_details` ×2) and `reinitializeViews`
  (context switch, config reload) send `TerminalFocusMsg{Focused: !a.terminalBlurred}` — always, so a view
  left while blurred does not keep a stale flag.
- Held views off screen receive nothing on the edges (H4).
- The layout is not re-measured (a focus message never changes a footer height).

**Tests to write first:**
1. `TestBlurTellsOnlyTheViewOnScreen`: two held `fakeView`s; blur → on-screen view received
   `TerminalFocusMsg{false,false}` (`receivedOf`), the other received nothing.
2. `TestFocusAsksTheViewOnScreenToResumeOnce`: blur, focus → on-screen view received exactly one
   `{true,true}`; `inits` unchanged; a second `FocusMsg` sends nothing.
3. `TestFocusWithoutBlurTellsNobody` (degradation): `FocusMsg` on a fresh router → no view received a
   `TerminalFocusMsg`, Cmd nil.
4. `TestAViewEnteringTheScreenIsToldTheFocus`: table — blurred / focused × `switchView`, path picker,
   selection entry → the entering view's last `TerminalFocusMsg` is `{Focused: !blurred, Resume: false}`.
5. `TestAContextSwitchWhileBlurredTellsTheRebuiltView`: blurred, `reinitializeViews()` → the new view on
   screen received `{false,false}`.
6. `TestFocusStartsNoScan` (Rule 126): blur, focus with a real `ws` view on screen (or `:sec`) → running
   the returned Cmd yields no `jobs.StartMsg`; `a.jobs.Snapshot()` length unchanged.

**Done when:** green; `go test ./internal/app ./internal/shared -count=1 -run 'Focus|Blur|Entering|Switch'`.

1. #362 (`feat/DEVDESK-210-focus-blur-animation`) : le terminal sans focus suspend l'animation (étape 1).

Après chaque merge, il faut repointer la PR suivante sur `main`.

**Ce que fait l'ensemble**
- `:agent-usage`, containers, Ports, dashboard et OCI sautent leurs relectures quand le terminal perd le focus. Leur tick continue et une lecture unique a lieu au retour du focus.
- L'en-tête d'`:agent-usage` affiche « Updates › paused (terminal not focused) », puis « Updates › live » au retour.
- Les jobs en cours ne sont jamais interrompus.
- Le nouveau réglage `app.when_unfocused` (`pause` par défaut, `run`) est modifiable dans `:cfg`.

**Vérifié**
- Sur la branche d'intégration, le `tester` a observé `mise run test` (77 paquets `ok`), `test-race` sans race, `lint` à 0 issue, et `-count=2` ciblé `ok`.

- J'ai corrigé dans #364 un bug existant : le rafraîchissement OCI de 10 s ne tournait qu'une fois. ### Publishing a release — release-please, then goreleaser

**A release takes two merges, and that is the point.** `release-please`
watches `main` and keeps a **release pull request** open: it reads the
conventional commits since the last tag, decides the version, and writes
`CHANGELOG.md`. Merging that PR creates the tag and the GitHub Release;
`goreleaser` then builds the six binaries (linux, darwin, windows × amd64,
arm64) and attaches them to that Release.

#### The flow, plainly — accumulate, then release whenever you want

The two actors: `release-please` **proposes** (it never writes directly to
`main` except through its own PR), `goreleaser` **builds**, and it only
triggers once that PR is merged. Concrete timeline:

1. A `fix:` or a `feat:` is merged onto `main` (a normal work PR, see
   above, in the `git-worktree-pr` skill, SKILL.md). The code ships right away. release-please sees that commit and
   **creates or updates** — never two PRs in parallel — the
   "chore(main): release x.y.z" PR with the corresponding changelog; that PR
   only touches `CHANGELOG.md` and `.release-please-manifest.json`.
2. Step 1 repeats as many times as wanted — several fixes, one or several
   features, over days or weeks. Each merge grows the same release PR (the
   version number can climb, a `feat:` bumps the minor) without any tag
   being set and without any binary being published.
3. When the moment is judged right — and only then — the release PR itself
   gets merged. That specific merge, and only that one, sets the tag,
   creates the GitHub Release, and wakes up goreleaser.

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| Merge a `fix:`/`feat:` onto `main` | Code shipped immediately; the release PR updates in the background; nothing is published |
| Merge the release PR | **Sole trigger for publishing** — tag, Release, binaries |

Publishing is therefore never a per-commit act: it is a deliberate act,
decided by merging a PR that already exists and that can be left to grow
indefinitely.

```bash
# nothing to run: the release PR opens and updates itself on its own
gh pr list -R anthnel/devdesk --label "autorelease: pending"
gh pr merge -R anthnel/devdesk <n> --squash   # ← this merge is what publishes
```

#### When to propose a release

Publishing is never automatic, but it should not be forgotten either. The `pm`
**proposes** merging the release PR at key moments; **the user alone decides**.
No agent merges the release PR without the user's explicit agreement.

Any one of these is enough to trigger a proposal:

1. **Story delivered**: a Plane story moves to Done (its `feat:`/`fix:` PR is merged on `main`).
2. **Module finished**: every story of a Plane module (epic) is Done.
3. **Security fix**: a fix touching security (auth, secrets, external input,
   vulnerable dependencies, image signatures) lands on `main`. Propose immediately.
4. **Accumulation**: the open release PR
   (`gh pr list -R anthnel/devdesk --label "autorelease: pending"`) holds at
   least 5 changelog entries, or 2 weeks have passed since the last release
   (`gh release list -R anthnel/devdesk --limit 1`).

A subagent never speaks on its own, so the check belongs to the session that
orchestrates (orchestrator, `/feature`, `/bugfix`): **after every merge on
`main`**, it evaluates the triggers above. If one is met, it delegates to the
`pm` to draft the proposal: proposed version, content (taken from the release
PR body), the trigger met, and anything still in progress that would justify
waiting. It then asks the user. On yes, `devops` merges the release PR; on no,
nothing happens and the PR keeps accumulating.

**Why not semantic-release**, which would achieve the same thing in a single
merge: it pushes the tag directly to `main`, and this repository forbids
that — the `main-protection` ruleset (id `22399372`: PR required, `Lint and build`
and `Test` green, no force-push) refuses it, and so does the Entire mirror
(see the `git-worktree-pr` skill, SKILL.md). One extra merge per release is the price of that rule.

**The mirror replicates tags, verified on 2026-09-06.** The tag is set by
GitHub Actions, so it is born on GitHub and not via the mirror — but
`git fetch origin --tags` brings it back, just as it brings back a
squash-merge done by `gh`. That was the only unknown in the chain, and it is
now resolved: nothing forces setting a tag by hand.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `release-please-config.json` | the type (`go`), the CHANGELOG sections |
| `.release-please-manifest.json` | the current version — **written by the bot**, never by hand |
| `.goreleaser.yaml` | the six targets, the `-ldflags`, `mode: append` |
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | the two jobs, chained by `release_created` |

**A repository setting no workflow can grant itself**: *Settings →
Actions → Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests*. Without
it, the first run fails on the PR it cannot open, and the message does not
say that is why. **Already active here** —
`gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/actions/permissions/workflow` answers
`can_approve_pull_request_reviews: true`, verified on 2026-09-06. The same
call shows `default_workflow_permissions: read`, which is not a problem:
that is the default when a workflow states nothing, and `release.yml`
declares its own.

**The binary's version comes from `-ldflags`**, not from a committed file
(§3.62). `release-please` knows how to write into a Go file (`versionFile`)
and it is not used for that: it would be a second source of truth for an
answer the build already gives, and a dev binary would then show the number
of the last release instead of `dev`.

**Before pushing a change to the chain**, `mise run release-check` validates
the configuration and `mise run release-snapshot` builds the six targets
without publishing anything — it is the only way to discover a broken target
before a tag is set.

**The first release will list the whole history** (66 `feat:` and 50 `fix:`
